fact: Gabon Media Time reports that the law ratifying the social-network ordinance, promulgated by decree 0436/PR of 5 October 2026, bans deepfakes of public or private persons (art. 32) and requires editors within 12 months to deploy AI-content detection and a visible, permanent label on AI-generated content (art. 53).

fact: Village de la Justice says Gabon's ordinance n°0011/PR/2026, signed 26 February 2026 and published in Journal Officiel n°110 of 8-15 April 2026, bans sexual deepfakes without consent and deepfakes attributing false statements to public figures, with a right to report and removal within 24 hours.

Village de la Justice says ordinance n°0013/PR/2026 gives the Haute Autorité de la Communication (HAC) express competence to regulate digital platforms, and that the HAC is given the task of auditing AI systems.
Global Voices, citing Gabon Review, says a law enacted on 5 October 2026 ratifies the social media ordinance and establishes a regulatory framework for AI-generated and AI-amplified content.

fact: Civicus Monitor reports that Ordinance n° 0011/PR/2026, adopted by the president on 26 February 2026 and immediately applicable, penalises AI-generated manipulations, particularly deepfakes made with malicious intent, with up to ten years' imprisonment.
